title: The German job seeker visa
description: Who can apply for a job seeker visa, what it allows, which documents the embassy expects and how it compares with the Opportunity Card.
html:
The job seeker visa lets qualified professionals enter Germany to look for work without a job offer in hand. It has been partly overtaken by the Opportunity Card, but it remains relevant, particularly for graduates of German universities. Here is how it works.

What the visa allows

A stay of up to six months to look for a job that matches your qualification. Graduates of German universities can get up to 18 months. Working during the search is not permitted on this visa, which is its main disadvantage compared with the Opportunity Card.

Who qualifies

You need a university degree or vocational qualification that is recognised in Germany, proof that you can support yourself during the search, health insurance and, in practice, a credible plan for finding work in your field. There is no points test.

Documents

  • Valid passport and the completed application form
  • Recognised qualification and proof of recognition (for example a printout from the Anabin database or a statement of comparability)
  • Proof of funds, usually a Blocked Account with the monthly amount set by the authorities for each month of the stay
  • Health insurance for the whole period
  • CV, cover letter and, if available, evidence of your job search
  • Proof of accommodation for the first period

The application

Since 2025, most applicants can submit the application through the online portal of the Federal Foreign Office, upload the documents and then attend the embassy in person for biometrics and payment. Processing takes several weeks to a few months depending on the embassy. Once you have a job, you apply at the local immigration office to switch to a work permit or an EU Blue Card.

Job seeker visa or Opportunity Card

The Opportunity Card runs for twelve months instead of six, allows part-time work of up to 20 hours a week and trial jobs, and can be obtained through a points system if your qualification is not fully recognised. For most applicants from abroad it is the better instrument. The job seeker visa still makes sense for graduates of German universities, who get the longer period, and for applicants who want the simpler route without points.
